title: The existing signed completed root line is intrinsically constructible and complete.
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $D$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and chosen uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and any scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible in every residue field. Write $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$, and $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ for the completed coefficient sheaf on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $L=\mathcal O_E(1)_W$ be the concrete completed integral root module of [def-pur-twist-sheaves]. Using sheaf tensor and sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pur-sheaf-hom], put
$$
L_m=\begin{cases}R,&m=0,\\ L^{\otimes_R m},&m>0,\\ \mathcal Hom_R(L^{\otimes_R(-m)},R),&m<0.\end{cases}
$$
For every $m\in\mathbf Z$, the degree-zero derived object $K_m=L_m[0]$ belongs to the intrinsic bounded constructible derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. In other words, its canonical derived reduction tower is derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete], and there exist $a\le b$ such that every derived reduction $K_m\otimes_R^L(A_n)_W$ is finite-torsion constructible [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] with cohomological support [def-weil-cohomological-support] contained in $[a,b]$, independently of $n$. Here one can take $a=b=0$. This is precisely $\operatorname{sfIntegralConstructible}(\ell,E,W)(K_m)$ for the published object $\operatorname{integralCoefficientTwist}(D,\ell,E,W,m)$; $D$ supplies the auxiliary parameter of that construction and imposes no structure morphism on $W$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NF-76f5cc613 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. Its statement matches the Lean intrinsicIntegralCoefficientTwist_mem: integralCoefficientTwist, the coefficientTwistLine cases m=0, m>0 and negSucc (sheaf Hom into the unit), and both halves of the sfIntegralConstructible conjunction. It adds no hypotheses and drops none. Small cases hold: m=0, ±1 and -2, n=1, an empty W and a non-quasi-compact W (W is open and retrocompact in itself, so the one-stratum split is constructible), and a ramified E. Each step's cited statement supplies what the step takes. Step 1: root local models give the pro-etale rank-one witness hL that the integral local models need, over the same ring R. Step 3: the line is K-flat, the derived change of rings is computed on q=id, and the well-definedness lemma matches the units and transitions with the canonical tower. Step 4: the absolute-value, DVR and finite-quotient lemmas, the constant-module encoding, finite-model stalks and a single stratum give constructibility. Step 5: limits are taken sectionwise, the cover-local isomorphism lemma applies, and the transition maps are epimorphisms locally. Step 6: the surjective-tower lemma (clauses 1-2) gives the triangle with first map c, and the legacy comparison turns it into IsSfDerivedComplete. Step 7: the single-support lemma gives constructibility and support in {0}, so a=b=0. No cited node reaches the item. The unit has uses [] and no steps, so the declared tool_uses are acceptable generic tools. Searching the DAG for this membership statement found no duplicate. FIX (C1): step 2 identified slice restrictions of sheaf tensor powers 'by definition'. That needs the existing lemma lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction, (F⊗G)|_U ≅ F|_U⊗G|_U.
